narrative:
Based on the information available, the model estimates a 27% chance that you would be a bad credit risk. While this means there is a 73% chance you would repay reliably, that 27% risk level is considered too high for the bank to approve, so your application was denied.

The single most important factor in this decision was the loan amount you requested: 11,054 DM. Approved applicants in this dataset ask for about 3,020 DM on average, making your request more than three and a half times the typical amount. A loan of this size represents a substantially larger obligation, and this is what pushed the prediction most strongly toward bad credit.

Interestingly, two other factors worked in your favor but were not enough to outweigh the large request. Your checking account status and your savings situation both pointed toward good credit. Having no checking account is actually the most common situation among approved applicants, and your savings pattern is also seen in a third of approved borrowers. These factors helped lower your risk score, but the sheer size of the requested loan remained the dominant reason for the denial.

The most realistic path forward is to apply for a significantly smaller loan amount. Reapplying with a request closer to the average for approved borrowers would remove the main reason for the denial. In the meantime, building up your savings or opening a checking account could further strengthen your application in the future.
